To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

α-defensin1-3 production was increased in dendritic cells (a cell type that is crucial in the first steps of the HIV infection) of HIV-infected patients and this increase was associated with better disease control.

α-defensin1-3 production was significantly increased by DC in elite and viremic controllers, compared to healthy controls and viremic noncontrollers, respectively, and that higher levels of α-defensin production by immature DC was associated with better immunological and virological parameters in HIV-infected patients.
increased production of α-definsins 1- 3 by immature dendritic cells in HIV-1 infected individuals is associated with slower disease progression.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and functional characterization of the innate immune response to HIV-1 infection.
the role of α-defensin1-3 production in DCs in controlling HIV infection, suggesting that this host protective mechanism might be a target for future therapeutic interventions.
the role of α-defensin1-3 as a host-protective factor against progression of the HIV infection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
α-defensin1-3 production in immature DCs may be an important host protective factor against HIV-1 disease progression.
high α-defensins production by DC is a marker for HIV control, and this effect is more pronounced in elite than in non-elite controllers.
the increased α-defensins 1–3 production by immature DC in HIV-infected patients is associated with a slower disease progression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
α-defensin1-3 is a protective factor for HIV-1 infection.
high α-defensins production by immature DC may contribute to the maintenance of the HIV reservoir, and hence to slow disease progression.
α-defensin1-3 produced by immature DCs may be a host protective factor in HIV-infected individuals.
The main takeaway from our work is that

α-defensin production by DC is an innate protective mechanism against HIV-1, and that the higher production of α-defensis1-3 by DC in elite controllers is a key factor in their ability to control viral replication.

α-defensin1-3 production may be used as a biomarker to identify individuals who may progress to AIDS, and that α-defenins1-3 may be used as an adjunctive therapy for the treatment and prevention of HIV-1 infection.
increased production of α-defenins by dendritic cells may be a marker of a more efficient immune response to HIV-1.
